chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, affliction and patience race toward the believer, so affliction comes to him while he is patient. And indeed, panic and affliction race toward the disbeliever, so affliction comes to him while he is panic-stricken.

key_terms.الصَّبْرَ: patience and steadfast endurance in the face of hardship
key_terms.الْبَلَاءَ: trial, affliction, or calamity that befalls a person
key_terms.الْجَزَعَ: panic, impatience, and distressed agitation at hardship
key_terms.الْكَافِرِ: the disbeliever, described here as meeting affliction with panic
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, characterized here by patient response to affliction
key_terms.جَزُوعٌ: one who is panic-stricken and unable to bear hardship calmly
key_terms.صَبُورٌ: patient and enduring in the moment of trial

ai.seo_question: How does a believer respond to trials according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the believer meets trials with sabr, while the disbeliever meets them with panic and agitation. It highlights patience as a defining moral and spiritual quality of iman when facing affliction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.528 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"Indeed, trials and patience race toward the believer, so when trials reach him, he is patient. But panic and trials race toward the disbeliever, so when trials reach him, he panics."
